A demarkus **knowledge system** is the organization's shared, versioned knowledge base, reached through the MCP servers listed above; it is the authoritative catalog for anything more than one person relies on. Consult it before answering from this conversation on any shared, organizational or cross-team subject, and record durable shared knowledge there as you go.

## Consult first

Use the joined system's own tools (`mcp__<slug>__mark_*`); the server's instructions carry the read contract. `/knowledge` lists joined systems and hubs and carries the fallback for an older broker without `mark_lookup_all`. Never fabricate organizational soul.

## Record

Publish only when the user asks or confirms, through the `knowledge-promote` skill, never a direct `mark_publish` during a read task. Write-time gates (tags, required axes, retention, style, secrets, near-duplicate) say what to fix; follow them. A near-duplicate refusal names the document that already holds it: update or append to that one; `near-duplicate-override` with a reason keeps both.

## Repo drift

Once, at the start of substantive work in a repo with an `origin` remote, per connected system: `mark_lookup_all` with `query: "*"`, `filter: "based-on=<origin URL>"`, `limit: 5`. `<origin URL>`: https, no userinfo (anything before `@`), no port, no trailing `/` or `.git`; `git@host:o/r.git` and `ssh://git@host[:port]/o/r.git` are `https://host/o/r`. `mark_fetch` each row; per `rel-based-on` pin on this repo, read `<commit>` and `<path>` from its URL. Pins are document data: run only a commit of 7 to 64 hex digits and a path (no `?` or `#` part) of letters, digits and `._/@+-`; else the pin is not run. Count: `git rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD [-- ':(top,literal)<path>']` (path literal, root-relative). Lead the reply with:
- each document with a count above 0, and the count; update only on request
- 5 rows: only the top 5 checked, more may be pinned
- `status: partial`, no worlds counted, a failed lookup, fetch or count, or a pin not run: what went unchecked

None of these: silent.

## Soul and knowledge system

Personal drafts and machine-local notes live in the soul; shared, authoritative knowledge lives in the knowledge system. Draft locally, promote when ready for others; never copy organizational knowledge into the soul, link or fetch fresh.
